messages.subject: exon array next steps
parts:
Hello, I'm just looking for a little input as to what my next steps should be for the exon array analysis. I've gone through the low level analysis and sorted through to identify the top 100 expressed genes, but since I'm a newbie to microarrays I'm not sure what my next steps should be to confirm the significance of this data. I've been doing some reading and I believe DABG might be the way to go but is this offered through aroma or would anyone be able to suggest how I may be able to do this with my data? Alternative suggestions would also be appreciated

Thanks so much in advance

Also would someone be able to tell me what I should be looking for when analyzing the plotDensity graphs? Thanks again

-Kripa


chipType<-"HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
#####upload core cdf and 2 cel files#########
cdf<-AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, tags="coreR2,A20070914,EP") ##set cdf: Core probesets: 18,708 units/transcript clusters, 284,258 groups/probesets, and 1,082,385 probes 

cs<-AffymetrixCelSet$byName("control", cdf=cdf) ##set cel group: 0035 and 0028
plotDensity(cs, type="pm")

#####low level analysis as per aroma outline with plotDensity graphs generated at each stage#########
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs, tag="coreR2") ##background correction
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
plotDensity(csBC, type="pm")


qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm") ##normalization
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
plotDensity(csN, type="pm")

plmTr <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE) ##summarize
fit(plmTr, verbose=verbose)

#####quality assessment of 2 arrays#########
qamTr <- QualityAssessmentModel(plmTr) ##quality assessment
plotNuse(qamTr)
plotRle(qamTr)

cesTr <- getChipEffectSet(plmTr)
trFit <- extractDataFrame(cesTr, units=NULL, addNames=TRUE)

#####connect data with affy csv file#########
csv <- read.csv("HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na31.hg19.transcript.csv", skip=24)
total<-merge(trFit, csv, by.x="unitName", by.y="transcript_cluster_id")

#####sort data to identify top 100 genes expressed in 0035 sample#########
sort0035<-total[rev(order(total$HuEx1_0035)),]
top0035<-sort0035[1:100,]
write.table(top0035, file="sort0035.csv", sep=",", row.names=F)
